example.title: Boston Street Bridge (Lakewood Avenue Drain Headwall and Bridge), Boston Street over the Harris Creek Sewer outlet

brief: City-built masonry arch of 1901-02: a 26.5 ft clear-span segmental arch about 70 ft long through the fill, with a barrel of several concentric brick rings, a ring of articulated granite voussoirs with a keystone chiselled with the date, and rock-faced granite ashlar headwalls and abutments on timber grillage and piles. It carries a wide industrial street (two 14 ft sidewalks, a 42 ft roadway and once a railway siding); the low stone parapet originally had an iron railing, later raised with a plain concrete parapet. Brick mill and warehouse buildings and a smokestack line the waterfront around it; one 1901 construction photo shows the brick rings on timber centering.

traits.railing_detail: low granite parapet raised with plain concrete (originally iron railing)
traits.masonry: brick barrel, granite voussoirs and rock-faced ashlar facing
